question: Cross-encoder reranking is described as more accurate than bi-encoder cosine similarity because it lets query and document attend to each other directly — what does that accuracy improvement actually cost a pipeline in milliseconds when reranking a typical shortlist?
answer:
The cross-encoder reranking process adds real, measurable latency compared to the near-instant cosine similarity lookup. For a typical shortlist of 20 to 50 candidates, this can add on the order of 100 to 300 milliseconds [chunk-id::1].

Specifically, chunk [chunk-id::1] states: "reranking even a modest shortlist of 20 to 50 candidates can add on the order of 100 to 300 milliseconds, depending on the cross-encoder's size and the hardware it runs on — this is the concrete cost side of the accuracy-versus-latency tradeoff introduced in the note on reranking with cross-encoders."
